title: Replicating Frontier Safety Framework Scoring with a Cheaper LLM-as-Judge Rubric

original_idea.body:
# Replicating Frontier Safety Framework Scoring with a Cheaper LLM-as-Judge Rubric

**Problem:** Expert scoring of company safety frameworks doesn't scale to frequent re-scoring; rubric inter-rater reliability is unestablished.

**Direction:** Operationalize the published rubric as an LLM-as-judge pipeline, run on the same public frameworks, measure agreement with human scores, stress-test reliability across prompt phrasing and model.

**Why it matters:** Cheap reproducible framework scoring is strategically valuable watchdog infrastructure.

**Relevant context:** Extends arXiv:2512.01166.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain (scalable framework scoring pressures labs) but the catastrophic-risk link is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Operationalize a rubric as an LLM-judge pipeline on public text; guided and tractable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused replication + agreement measurement; few dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Pure-text watchdog infrastructure any external party can run; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: LLM-judge over public frameworks; single mid GPU or API.

novelty.reasoning: The human-rated study exists; the LLM-judge replication + reliability test is the open extension.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Human scoring exists; automated replication and reliability testing is the open extension.
